reviews.comment: This class is genuinely difficult, and you cannot study for its last minute. However, Professor Sze is very caring and makes the class doable.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 6 homeworks, 3 exams. Grades leniently (-2 points out of 10 per question for entirely wrong answers as long as you're applying the topics). Lectures are alright, topics can get a bit confusing but recordings are uploaded to canvas. Easy to make a B at least, but not a free A.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sing is a kind professor and is usually very generous with grading. Almost impossible to get < B. However, his teaching style is difficult to follow and understand. There were no TAs or "Week-in-reviews" like the regular math classes. Therefore, I did not enjoy the class, and if I were given the chance, I would not take this class again.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would 100% recommend this class. As long as you take your time on the homework he assigns you, you will get a good grade. Attendance is not mandatory, and he releases his lectures on Canvas. Very, and I mean Very lenient on grading. The only downside to this class was that his handwriting was difficult to read.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to try to get a B in this class, there are 6 homeworks (30%) and 3 exams (70%) all of which are just 5 free response questions. Some content at the end of the class is challenging but grading for everything is very lenient, he is strict about being formal but rarely takes off more than 5 points even for a completely wrong answer.
Goat Sze. Never gives you below an 80 as long as you are using the correct method. Material is alright until the end where it gets kinda hard. Besides that, the actual goat.
goat activity

Great professor!!  This course was super interesting, and Professor Sze made the computational analysis understandable to someone with no previous background.  Although the lectures were recorded, it was still beneficial to go to class, and the professor was great at answering questions.  He also always took the time to go over homework/exam keys.

He grades extremely leniently, but I was unable to learn much from his lectures. I got an A by memorizing the practice tests without actually understanding the material. I wish I actually learned something.

6 HWs and 3 Tests. Lectures are recorded. He sends both the recordings and lecture notes via email. You have to try to get a B. Takes off at most 2 points for wrong answers. First three homeworks were easy. It only got difficult towards the end in terms of concepts. H does have an accent but rewatching the lectures helped. Take him or Dr. Carlisle.

Explains things well if you pay attention. I learned a lot. He grades very lenient for a baseline but is harsh towards getting perfect scores. Almost impossible to get below a B.  Tests are fair. 

Con: In later concepts. There weren't that many practice problems with solution sets given, which can make it hard to train yourself.
While I personally found the class to be difficult, Professor Sze was amazing. The grades is even

Sing is BY FAR the best 222 prof. It is pretty much impossible to get below a B and an A is super achievable. He is very passionate about the subject. The tests are basically an easier version of the hw + he sends out previous hw to study. Notes AND lecture video are posted online (do with this what you will...)

You really have to try to get below a B in Dr. Sze's class. Lectures can be somewhat fast and confusing, but his grading criteria makes up for it in my opinion. Tests are very very similar to hwks. Would recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was nervous about this class at the beginning but turns out there's nothing to worry about. He is super nice and responds to emails fast. His lectures are so on point with recordings and notes available. Homework's a bit challenging but exams will be easier and he grades so leniently. Love this prof I want all my classes with him :D

Great professor. Grading is very lenient. Lectures are recorded and the notes he writes during the class are emailed out so you can review on your own time which I really appreciated. Material starts easy and gets complex towards the end of the class, but exams and homeworks are very fair.

Extremely knowledgeable professor who clearly has a deep understanding of Computability Theory. All lectures are recorded and posted online. Six homeworks with a very clear grading criteria with three exams which are similar to the homeworks. Learned a lot in this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very friendly professor who has a strong understanding of the class he teaches. Lenient grader who gives great feedback on HW and exams so students can correct their mistakes. Explains concepts intuitively and concisely
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's hard to reach outside of class, emails will go unanswered. However, he's easy to approach or find in his office. Very lenient with grading, you have to try to fail this class. The lectures are underwhelming but he is clear with information and class materials are given afterwards. Everything is handwritten and his handwriting is NOT good :)

He's your best chance at getting an A in 411. His notes are pretty confusing, exams even more confusing, and homework the most confusing, but read his lecture notes and kinda argue for points back on assignments and you'll be fine

He gives his lectures by writing on paper with a pen and pointing a camera at it. It's hard to read and he doesn't move the camera. Also, he doesn't teach the material very well and you'll probably be confused and not learn much. Still, he grades extremely leniently and you're pretty much guaranteed an A unless you don't turn in assignments.

This class had six assignments (60%) and two exams (40%). Dr. Sze was a very generous grader and willing to help you with the assignments. Lectures can be confusing at times but the exams were very similar to the assignments.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sze is a good professor and is often lenient with grading. I found the home works to be hard, but the grading was not hard as long as you attempted to use what you learned in class. He is unconventional and does not use any online resources, so you have to go to class to get your graded papers and calculate a grade yourself.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Dr. Sze delivers the content in a very straightforward and well organized way, and really knows his stuff. There are only 6 HWs during the semester (5% each), and 3 exams with 5-8 questions. He's a very lenient grader so as long as you even kind of understand, you'll probably end up with an A or a B. 

Overall a GOAT and highly recommend!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The GOAT. It's plain and simple the GOAT of 222. The only criticism I have is that the HWs were definitely difficult but gave a great understanding of the concept and towards the end I wished that there were more examples and that the pacing slowed down.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was pretty happy with Dr. Sze's teaching for the most part. He doesn't add a lot of fluff. There were a few concepts I felt he could have explained better (like generating functions), but overall it wasn't too bad. He is a very lenient grader, so that helped a lot.

As long as you pay attention in class and understand the 6 homework pages he gives for the whole semester, it's impossible to fail. He explains concepts intuitively, writes all his notes on printer paper and emails them, the pacing is quick (not boring), his grading is generous, and typically the exam questions are always easier than the homework.

Prof. Sze taught 222 very well, he made it an interesting class and communicated the concepts very easily. The notes are excellent, the grading was very generous. The notes made the homework easy which made the tests easy, and Prof. Sze organized things very well and clearly.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! The content was pretty tough, especially the homeworks, but they prepare you well for the exams. I strongly recommend knowing how to do all of the homework problems for the exams (exams usually have easier versions of homework problems). Definitely recommend - super awesome guy!

Dr. Sze is very straightforward, which is perfect. His entire syllabus fit on a half sheet of paper and he immediately dove into the content on Day 1. His grading is very lenient and he is very straightforward about what he is looking for. He never set up canvas though so be sure to save your papers. 

100% recommend you take him for 222.

Dr. Sze is a great teacher that aims to give you a deep understanding of discrete maths. He is expectant of performance but doesn't make overly difficult tests. Homeworks are difficult but you have well over a week for each one, and you can finish it if you pay attention in lecture and understand the notes. He also does not use any online portals.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As long as you can generally get the concepts, he will at the very least give you a B. He gives so much partial credit that it would be very, very difficult to get below a B in this class. But I don't think he was good at explaining the topics. He goes way too quickly on a pretty confusing class, but his grading makes up for it very much.
I entered the class filled with doubts, fears ,and uncertainty. I now leave this class with a new perspective in life and a purpose to live. Thank you Dr. Sze, you are the real MVP.
Before I took his class, my IQ was average at best. However, after being blessed by the god that is Professor Sze, my IQ has soared well above Einstein's. #singhoi for president

Dr. Sze is a nice enough guy, but honestly not a great professor. He's assumed to be really easy - and he usually is, but honestly, his grading is just all over the place and since he doesn't use eCampus it is even harder to determine where you stand.
Friendly Professor who clarifies every doubt
Dr. Sze is an amazing professor for CSCE 222. He has great lectures and is VERY knowledgeable on the subject he teaches.

Go to class, all lecture material is written on a whiteboard. He is a VERY generous grader, and the few HWK's that he does have are easy if you follow your notes from class (The lecture examples similar to the HWK problems). For the exams, study and practice the HWK problems and it is very likely you can pull an A. Best choice of prof for CSCE-222.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely the best professor for 222. You have to go to lecture because he does all his notes by hand and doesn't post them online. If you pay attention and actually try the homework, it is an easy A. He was very good about reviewing before tests and really tried to make sure that we understood the material. He also didn't make us buy the textbook

This prof is one of my favorites. His lectures are engaging and he always shows up well prepared for class. He doesn't rely on powerpoints like other profs. He makes this subject easier to understand. He grades easily too. YOU HAVE TO GO TO CLASS. He handwrites everything and doesn't post it online. I would recommend him to anyone taking CSCE 222.

An easy A as long as you show up to class and ask questions. There are 6 homework assignments throughout the semester, and each one is given at least a week before being due. The assignments only have 5 problems each, and are simple enough that you can answer them easily. Test questions are easier than homework. You will actually learn the material
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious
